# History and evidence distinctions

Adopt the proposed meanings of occurrence, event, state, observation, record and evidence in [the history page](../../standard/ontology/concepts/occurrences-and-state.md#what-happened-what-was-observed-and-what-was-recorded). An occurrence is a particular happening; an event is an occurrence relevant to the model. A state describes conditions of a subject at a time. An observation is the act of examining or measuring, distinct from its result. A record is retained information representing or claiming something. Evidence is information used to support or challenge an identified claim.

These meanings may overlap and do not require separate document types. Require separate representations of event and occurrence only when the distinction is useful. This accepts the terminology and representation recommendation presented in the conversation; it does not close EOM-06/F6 or accept the remaining time, inference, correction and minimum-context proposals by implication.
